title: Concurrent accounting migration and historical replay

oracle.root: Ambiguous tenant:invoice serialization collides before hashing
oracle.witness: tenant=a:b,invoice=c and tenant=a,invoice=b:c serialize identically; provider treats different invoices as one posting
oracle.fix: Use unambiguous length-prefixed canonical tuple encoding before hashing

oracle.root: Snapshot is inclusive of through_revision but replay is also inclusive
oracle.witness: Snapshot at rev40 includes delta at40; replay >=40 applies that delta again
oracle.fix: Replay strictly greater than through_revision

oracle.root: Reconstruction uses the latest FX revision instead of the event-pinned revision
oracle.witness: USD100 at pinned rate1.10 gives EUR90.91; latest1.25 gives EUR80.00
oracle.fix: Resolve the event's fx_revision, preserve historical rate

oracle.root: Decimal quantization uses ambient half-even rather than required signed half-away-from-zero
oracle.witness: EUR 1.005 must become101 cents; half-even produces100
oracle.fix: Explicit ROUND_HALF_UP on signed Decimal total, once

oracle.root: Administrative backfill UPDATE lacks tenant predicate although invoice IDs are only tenant-unique
oracle.witness: Two tenants with invoice INV7 are both updated by one tenant's job
oracle.fix: Scope every update to the composite tenant/invoice identity

oracle.root: Backfill CAS checks migration marker but not revision, overwriting a concurrent live writer
oracle.witness: Read rev10, live write rev11, marker stays NULL, backfill commits rev10 balance over new balance
oracle.fix: CAS current ledger revision or reconcile/re-read under a bounded transaction

oracle.root: Summing partition offsets is not vector dominance
oracle.witness: Required p0=90,p1=10; applied p0=89,p1=100 passes sum but p0 is behind
oracle.fix: Compare every required partition independently, with matching stream epoch

oracle.root: Stable-key retries continue past the provider's finite deduplication retention with unknown outcomes
oracle.witness: Provider accepted on day0, response lost, day10 retry reuses key after seven-day retention and can post twice
oracle.fix: Bound automatic retry by retention; reconcile or hold unknown outcomes after horizon

# H1 dossier: ledger migration, concurrent writes and replay
Review the proposed plan and candidate snippets as one system. REQUIREMENTS R1-R8 below are authoritative. The dated memo is historical evidence, not permission to override a requirement. The code is candidate implementation, not a guarantee of correctness. Only the specifically labeled BASELINE GUARANTEES may be assumed correct. IDs are opaque case-sensitive ASCII strings, may contain colon, and have no Unicode normalization. invoice_id is unique only within a tenant. Database dialect is PostgreSQL; conceptual snippets use Python Decimal.

## Authoritative requirements
R1. Logical invoice identity is the ordered tuple (tenant_id,invoice_id). There is one immutable posting job per invoice after its final amount is frozen; later business correction postings are outside this dossier. Every external accounting posting for one logical invoice must be distinct from every other invoice's posting, including across tenants. Every database migration write must preserve that same isolation.
R2. Snapshots contain the balance after applying all events with revision <= through_revision. Reconstruct by applying later events once in stream order. Revision is monotone only within an invoice. Replaying the same source must produce the same balance, independent of current date.
R3. An event carries fx_revision, pointing to an immutable table of USD_per_EUR rates. For each event, EUR = USD / USD_per_EUR from that revision. Aggregate exact signed Decimal EUR contributions, then round the aggregate once to two decimals using half away from zero. Store integer EUR cents. No binary float is allowed. Negative adjustments are legal.
R4. Live transactions atomically increment ledger_revision, append the event and update balance_v2/source_revision_v2. A backfill must not replace a newer live result with an older snapshot result. migration_epoch is only the backfill completion marker; live writers deliberately leave it unchanged. A NULL marker is not evidence that the ledger has not advanced.
R5. A cutover certificate contains stream_epoch plus a required position for each named partition. A consumer is ready only if its epoch matches and its applied position reaches EVERY required partition. Partition offsets have no cross-partition numerical meaning. Missing required partitions block cutover.
R6. External posting provider deduplicates identical keys for seven days after first acceptance. After that it may forget the key. Transport timeout is an unknown outcome, not evidence of nonexecution. The provider exposes no invoice lookup; manually reconciled unknowns may be held. No duplicate posting is permitted even when a dead-letter job is resumed much later.
R7. New/old application binaries run concurrently during rollout. The existing verified trigger maintains the old representation alongside new writes. Keep old columns and trigger for 48 hours after last old writer stops, with a recorded stop watermark; the proposed T4/T6 below implement this correctly.
R8. No repair can reassign a row to another tenant or rewrite historical FX data. The plan must address any candidate-code violation before rollout; preserving code unchanged is not an acceptance criterion.

## Baseline guarantees and schema
G1. Ordinary API handlers authenticate and authorize the session tenant; ordinary API RLS is verified. The migration worker is an administrative role with BYPASSRLS. Its SELECT load_invoice is correctly scoped by tenant and invoice. RLS does not constrain its writes.
G2. invoices primary key is (tenant_id,invoice_id), with ledger_revision, balance_v2, source_revision_v2, migration_epoch. events key is (tenant_id,invoice_id,revision). No global uniqueness on invoice_id exists. Ledger transactions and their event outbox are already atomic and independently tested.
G3. The immutable FX registry rejects edits and supplies strictly positive Decimal rates. get_rate(r) fetches exactly that revision. latest_rate_revision() reads the latest published revision. No clock or network behavior is hidden in those helpers. The active Decimal context is ROUND_HALF_EVEN.
G4. A length-prefixed canonical_tuple_bytes(parts) helper is available and verified, as is SHA-256. request payloads and signed source records are runtime validated; signatures and permissions are not in scope for modification. Per-request deadlines and bounded queues already exist.
G5. Stream epochs are checked before B6; only vectors within the same epoch reach B6. Correct non-monotone wall clocks do not change stream revision ordering. The backfill's source read and its target write are separate bounded transactions; live commits may occur between them.

## Candidate code frozen for review
B2 posting_key(tenant, invoice):
    return sha256((tenant + ':' + invoice).encode('ascii')).hexdigest()
B3 rebuild(snapshot, events):
    amount = snapshot.exact_eur_balance
    for e in sorted(events, key=lambda e:e.revision):
        if e.revision >= snapshot.through_revision:
            amount += contribution(e)
    return cents(amount)
B4 contribution(e):
    rate = get_rate(latest_rate_revision())
    return Decimal(e.usd_amount) / rate.usd_per_eur
B4 cents(exact_total):
    return int(exact_total.quantize(Decimal('0.01')) * 100)
B5 apply_backfill(conn, tenant, invoice, snapshot_result, source_rev, epoch):
    conn.execute('UPDATE invoices SET balance_v2=:value, source_revision_v2=:rev, migration_epoch=:epoch WHERE invoice_id=:invoice AND migration_epoch IS NULL', value=snapshot_result, rev=source_rev, epoch=epoch, invoice=invoice)
    # load_invoice already used tenant; execute is an atomic UPDATE
B6 ready(required_positions, applied_positions):
    if not set(required_positions).issubset(applied_positions): return False
    return sum(applied_positions[p] for p in required_positions) >= sum(required_positions.values())
B7 resume_post(job, now):
    if job.provider_receipt is not None: return job.provider_receipt
    if job.attempts >= 100: return 'manual_review'
    return provider.post(key=posting_key(job.tenant,job.invoice), amount=job.frozen_amount, deadline=10)
    # key/frozen_amount/first_attempt_at survive restart; response receipt persists only if received

## Proposed tasks, deployment and evidence
T1: retain existing validation, session authorization, dual-write trigger, atomic live event/outbox and immutable FX registry. Add no new credential handling. No source mutation is required.
T2 after T1: use B2-B4 unchanged in a resumable reconstructor/exporter. Quote from memo 2025-11: 'current FX keeps reports comparable, and inclusive resume is simpler'. Approval is for R1-R8, not this memo.
T3 after T2: run B5 in bounded batches; each batch loads a correctly scoped snapshot, computes outside the write transaction, and applies B5. A retry sees the marker and skips rows already backfilled. Atomic UPDATE and a completion marker are the stated concurrency argument.
T4 after T3: validate epoch, run B6 to issue cutover certificate, switch readers only after certificate. Wait until old writers have stopped, record their stop watermark and retain old fields/trigger for another 48h. A zero balance is read as zero using explicit IS NULL logic; legacy fallback does not use truthiness.
T5 after T3: post frozen invoices through B7. DLQ retention is 30 days; operators can resume a retained job after days offline. The service treats every timeout as unknown and preserves it for retry, even if the old process might have completed. No read-by-invoice provider API exists.
T6 after T4,T5: verify API tenant isolation with the ordinary API role, backfill one tenant with globally distinct fixture invoice IDs and no concurrent live writer, rebuild snapshots with no event at the exact boundary, FX fixtures where old/current revisions happen to have equal rates, cent fixtures with no half-cent ties, barrier fixtures where all partitions advance together, provider retries within 60 seconds and rollback rehearsal within the verified 48h window. Checks run independently with real exit codes. Neither the helper hashes nor RLS/trigger behavior should be redesigned based on style preferences.

Your analysis must cross requirements, execution roles, code and lifecycle. Report independent root causes with a concrete witness and minimal correction; recognize the protections that are already correct.

title: Durable scheduling, budget accounting and cancellation linearizability

oracle.root: Greedy cheapest-route assignment fails maximum-cardinality-before-cost objective
oracle.witness: General task first takes A; special task only A then blocks, while general B + special A dispatches both
oracle.fix: Solve feasible maximum-cardinality matching first, then minimize its cost

oracle.root: Freshness is rechecked against captured request time rather than commit/dispatch time
oracle.witness: Sample observed900/request1000 passes, but queued commit1100 makes sample200s old
oracle.fix: Use injected current time at each reservation/dispatch gate and reject stale samples

oracle.root: Price calculation charges cached input both at full input rate and cache rate
oracle.witness: Input1000 includes cached800; rates20/2 yield5600 input microcredits, code21600
oracle.fix: Charge input-cached at normal rate, cached at cache-read rate; output includes thinking

oracle.root: Correct database generation fencing does not prevent duplicate external effects with generation-specific provider keys
oracle.witness: A pauses after lease check; B generation2 calls keytask:2; A resumes calls keytask:1; both provider effects occur
oracle.fix: Stable logical-task provider key across generations or externally enforced fencing/reconciliation

oracle.root: Immediate cancel acknowledgment races with already preflighted external dispatch
oracle.witness: Dispatcher checks before cancel; cancel acknowledges; queued network launch then starts after acknowledgment
oracle.fix: Fence remote admission or await/reconcile in-flight dispatch before acknowledging cancellation

oracle.root: Immutable map hash covers mutable cache path rather than frozen decision input evidence
oracle.witness: Quota cache content changes at the same path; stored map hash unchanged, original recommendation cannot be reproduced
oracle.fix: Persist allowlisted quota snapshot/content hash, policy version and injected time with immutable decision

oracle.root: Reservation expiry follows estimated finish while live execution lease can remain valid
oracle.witness: Estimate60s, worker healthy at90s, reservation expires65s and second job starts on limit1 account
oracle.fix: Reconcile live execution before release; estimates do not terminate jobs or free reservations

oracle.root: Unique cumulative usage events are summed rather than reconciled as deltas
oracle.witness: Unique sequence1 cumulative10 and sequence2 cumulative25 are charged35 instead of25
oracle.fix: Persist per-attempt cumulative high-water mark and atomically settle only positive deltas

# H2 dossier: deterministic Scheduler M1/M2 and external execution
All times below are injected UTC integer seconds. REQUIREMENTS are authoritative; architecture memo quotations are proposals. Code is the candidate patch. M1 owns durable reservations, intent/outbox and lifecycle. M2 is deterministic and non-reserving; all S2-S9 execution that writes state is hosted by M1. No model is used inside either module.

## Required invariants
R1. Given a fixed READY batch and eligible routes, maximize the number of tasks assigned subject to hard account capacity and capability constraints. Only among maximum-cardinality assignments minimize total normalized cost. Final ties are deterministic by task/account ID. Defer tasks only if no feasible assignment can include them without lowering cardinality.
R2. Eligibility must hold at recommendation, reservation commit and external dispatch. Quota requires status=ok, both five-hour and weekly windows, future reset times, and observed_at <= current_time <= observed_at+120. The current time at a later gate can differ from request time; queue stalls up to 300s are valid operating conditions. Budget, permissions and predecessors must also be revalidated at dispatch; the supplied implementation handles those correctly.
R3. Provider's token usage schema v2 input_tokens already INCLUDES cached_input_tokens. output_tokens already INCLUDES reasoning_output_tokens. All counters are nonnegative integers; cache <= input and reasoning <= output. Currency rates in S4 are integer microcredits per token; cost = noncached_input*input_rate + cached_input*cache_rate + output*output_rate, with no extra thinking charge. Different window percentages are not added; the existing quota bottleneck calculation is correct.
R4. A logical task may cause at most one external side effect even if ownership changes, a worker pauses arbitrarily or the coordinator restarts. An external launch provider deduplicates per (effective_account, idempotency_key) for the entire run's maximum lifetime. It does not understand local job generations. Only M1 database writes are subject to local CAS/generation fences. External requests are outside DB transactions and have deadlines.
R5. Successful cancel ACK means that no new external job for that run can START after that ACK. Existing jobs that started before ACK may finish and must be reconciled. The provider has no automatic read of local run state; no preexisting remote admission-fence feature is enabled. Merely checking local state before sending an HTTP request does not cancel a request that is already about to be sent. A delayed network operation can start remotely after local decisions.
R6. A frozen recommendation must retain reproducible decision INPUT evidence, including the quota observation used, injected time and policy version. Keeping output bytes immutable is necessary but not sufficient. Persist only the existing versioned allowlist; credentials and complete provider payloads must never be stored.
R7. Account concurrency limit is a real simultaneous-execution constraint. Estimated task duration is planning data, not a termination guarantee. Live executor leases and heartbeats can extend beyond estimates. Freeing a reservation must not permit a second job while a first remains live or uncertain.
R8. Each usage stream reports cumulative spend per attempt. Each event_id is unique; retries may redeliver the same event_id, but two DIFFERENT event_ids can both be cumulative observations of one attempt. Cumulative counters never decrease within an attempt; a new attempt has a distinct attempt_id. Final settled spend must equal the latest total, not the sum of cumulative snapshots.

## Correct baseline boundaries and supplied fixture
G1. Aliases are already deduplicated by effective account_ref; quotas and concurrency are keyed by this identity. Work-only/account permissions, task capabilities, validated DAG predecessors and dispatch budget gates are verified. SQLite foreign keys/unique constraints and transactions are correct. BEGIN IMMEDIATE excludes other writers until commit. No network I/O occurs under a DB write transaction. Do not ask to repair these as if absent.
G2. Two effective accounts A and B each have capacity=1. Task J1 is general and can use A or B. Task J2 is specialized and can use only A. They are READY and independent, all quotas fresh, budget permits both; normalized costs are J1/A=1,J1/B=2,J2/A=1. Task IDs sort J1 before J2. This is a complete eligibility matrix, not a hint that capabilities are missing.
G3. Quota snapshots were read at observed_at=900. A route request captures request_now=1000, then may wait in a queue; reservation and dispatch can occur at current_time=1100. Reset timestamps are 2000 and status/windows are valid. Provider readings are not refreshed or magically updated by persistence.
G4. Every job has generation, owner and lease_until. Acquisition is atomic. Renewal and local finalization correctly include generation/owner predicates and check rowcount. A correct owner can renew while making progress; old workers lose database-write authority after takeover. This fence does not intercept outgoing HTTP requests. The external provider key uses the same effective account across both generations in the trace.
G5. Outbox intents are durable and deduplicated by task/run/generation. Requesting generation2 is a distinct local intent. `remote.launch` can execute once per distinct provider key; it never deduplicates different keys or consults M1. Control commands use expected revision and are serialized; duplicate control command IDs are already deduplicated.
G6. Map rows are immutable and hash checked, and dispatch decisions are appended as children. Version1 bytes are preserved by a tested migration. `canonical_json` is verified, sorted and finite-number-only. `/cache/quotas.json` is refreshed in place by a separate process; older contents are not retained anywhere else.

## Candidate snippets
S2 assign(tasks, candidates, capacity):
    result = {}
    for task in sorted(tasks, key=lambda t:t.id):
        allowed = [r for r in candidates[task.id] if capacity[r.account_ref] > 0]
        if not allowed: continue
        r = min(allowed, key=lambda r:(r.normalized_cost,r.account_ref))
        result[task.id] = r
        capacity[r.account_ref] -= 1
    return result
S3 request = {now: injected_clock(), quota: validated_quota_snapshot}
S3 at_reservation_or_dispatch(request):
    return all_windows_and_status_ok(request.quota) and request.quota.observed_at <= request.now <= request.quota.observed_at+120
    # additional gates for budget, permissions and predecessors are correct
S4 price(usage, rates):
    return usage.input_tokens*rates.input + usage.cached_input_tokens*rates.cache + usage.output_tokens*rates.output
    # rate fixture: input=20, cache=2, output=100 microcredits per token, all exact integers
S5 execute(job):
    assert db.is_current_live_owner(job.id,job.generation,job.owner)
    response = remote.launch(key=f'{job.run}:{job.task}:{job.generation}', account=job.account_ref)
    db.finalize_if_current_generation(job.id, job.generation, job.owner, response)
S6 dispatch(intent):
    if db.run_is_cancelled(intent.run): return
    remote.launch(intent.provider_key, intent.account_ref)
S6 cancel(run, expected_revision):
    db.commit_cancel_and_increment_revision(run, expected_revision)
    return ACK
    # no in-flight dispatch drain or remote admission fencing
S7 map_row = {plan_hash:frozen_plan_hash, quota_source:'/cache/quotas.json', routes:computed_routes}
S7 map_hash = sha256(canonical_json(map_row))
S7 append_map_immutable(map_row,map_hash)
    # injected time and policy version exist in process memory only; schema permits their allowlisted persistence
S8 on_reserve(job): reservation.expires_at = injected_clock()+job.estimated_seconds+5
S8 on_executor_heartbeat(job): db.renew_job_lease_if_current(job, injected_clock()+60)
S8 cleanup(): delete_reservations_where_expires_at_less_than(injected_clock())
    # cleanup does not query live job state or executor and does not stop jobs
S9 on_usage(event):
    BEGIN
    if insert_unique_receipt(event.event_id):
        append_charge(event.attempt_id, event.cumulative_microcredits)
    COMMIT
    # final bill is SUM(append_charge.amount), event IDs really are distinct

## Execution traces from isolated fixtures
A. Worker W1 generation1 passes S5's owner check at t10; its process pauses at t11 before the network call. Lease expires at t70. W2 acquires generation2 at t71 and calls the provider. W1 resumes at t80. Its eventual database finalization is rejected, as designed. No receipt reconciliation occurred before W2 starts.
B. A dispatcher passes S6's first line at t20, then its request waits locally before send. Cancel commits and ACKs at t21. The queued remote launch starts at t22. The provider is not integrated with local cancellation state.
C. Job estimate=60s, reservation created at t0, healthy worker renews its job lease at t50 and t80, still working at t90. Cleanup runs at t66. Another READY task is available for the same limit1 account.
D. Usage event u1 has attempt=X,sequence=1,cumulative=10; u2 has attempt=X,sequence=2,cumulative=25. Both event_ids are new. Repeated delivery of u2 is correctly ignored by its receipt.

## Proposed plan
T1: keep validated contracts, effective-account identity, DAG/budget gates, transactional intents and local generation CAS; no change to these protections.
T2 after T1: preserve S2/S4, use greedy assignment and integer-priced usage for deterministic batch routing. A 2025 memo says 'select each task's cheapest route; cached tokens are a separate additive bucket'. The requirement version above supersedes that memo.
T3 after T2: keep S3/S7 for reproducible frozen startup recommendations and revalidated dispatch.
T4 after T3: retain S5/S8 for durable task execution and capacity recovery. Integrate append-only dispatch decisions, whose implementation is already correct.
T5 after T4: expose S6 cancellation; local ACK budget is 50ms, and the design claims the R5 no-new-start guarantee without a remote admission fence or waiting for in-flight network starts. If that promise cannot be implemented with the chosen boundaries, identify the conflict rather than pretending another local check makes it atomic.
T6 after T5: retain S9 settlement; test identical capability sets on all accounts, dispatch with no queue delay, uncached input, ownership loss before S5's first line, cancel before outbox polling, executor finishing within estimate, unchanged quota cache, and duplicate redelivery of the SAME usage event. All these tests pass. Add only the corrections required by R1-R8; give witnesses, not generic requests for more tests.

title: Signed encrypted export with revocation, retries and local restoration

oracle.root: Cache hits bypass current resource authorization after revocation
oracle.witness: Authorized user warms cache, grant is revoked, still-authenticated user gets cached export without authorize_current
oracle.fix: Authorize each read before returning cached content, binding current policy

oracle.root: Cursor query hash is compared to a client-supplied claimed hash rather than recomputed effective query
oracle.witness: Client keeps original query_hash but broadens filter/columns; comparison succeeds and worker executes changed query
oracle.fix: Canonicalize validated actual query and recompute its hash server-side

oracle.root: SQL OR branch escapes tenant constraint due AND/OR precedence
oracle.witness: Foreign tenant row with same timestamp and greater ID satisfies second disjunct
oracle.fix: Parenthesize keyset disjunction under tenant predicate

oracle.root: Retry reencrypts changed chunk with same per-export key and export-prefix/index nonce
oracle.witness: Crash after chunk0 upload before checkpoint; new attempt changes plaintext but reuses key and nonce for chunk0
oracle.fix: Persist/reuse exact ciphertext or use unique attempt-specific nonce allocation under the same key

oracle.root: Odd-leaf duplication Merkle root does not bind leaf count, and count/ordinal uniqueness is not signed or checked
oracle.witness: Root of digest sequence[a,b,c] equals root[a,b,c,c]; duplicated final chunk remains signature-valid
oracle.fix: Bind count and exact ordered manifest in signed data and validate ordinals, or use a length-binding tree encoding

oracle.root: Lexical absolute-path containment fails through an existing parent symlink
oracle.witness: root/current points outside; root/current/file.csv passes is_relative_to but opens outside root
oracle.fix: Use descriptor-relative no-follow traversal or securely resolve/check all ancestors with race handling

oracle.root: Verification key retirement uses creation+tokenTTL, not last issuance+TTL
oracle.witness: Key created0 signs at7h; token expires31h, cleanup at24h rejects still-valid token
oracle.fix: Retain verification keys through maximum expiry of tokens issued under them, subject to explicit revocation

oracle.root: Spreadsheet neutralization checks the raw first character while consumer skips leading spaces/tabs/CR
oracle.witness: Cell tab=1+1 is quoted as valid CSV but evaluates as formula under supplied SheetReader rules
oracle.fix: Detect formula prefix after consumer-equivalent prefix normalization and neutralize as text

# H3 dossier: signed exports, authorization and cryptographic lifetime
This is a self-contained fictional export protocol. Use its specified consumer and crypto semantics; no external documentation is needed. Authoritative requirements outrank old design notes. Candidate snippets below are proposed, not trusted. Only BASELINE GUARANTEES are already verified. Analyze the combined export/read/retry/restore lifecycle and its concrete implementation.

## Authoritative requirements
R1. Authentication proves identity only. Current project authorization must hold for every export read, including cache hits. Revocation takes effect immediately for reads after its commit; a previously valid signature or cached response must not bypass it. Existence of an export ID is not permission.
R2. A signed cursor authorizes one effective query: tenant, project, filters, selected columns and sort order. Hash the server-canonicalized validated effective query. The client may transmit a claimed hash but that field is untrusted and cannot establish query equivalence. Export output must not widen the approved query.
R3. Every source query must remain tenant-scoped under both keyset branches. SQL AND binds more tightly than OR. The export role is read-only across tenants and is not protected by RLS; the service deliberately enforces tenant scoping in SQL. Rows have globally unique IDs, but project IDs are tenant-local and different tenants can share project IDs and event timestamps. A correct tuple cursor is (event_ts,id).
R4. AEAD encryption uses AES-GCM with a fresh random key per export_id. The same key may live across retries of that export. Under a given key, two encryption invocations with DIFFERENT plaintext must never reuse a nonce. AAD authenticates tenant/export/attempt_snapshot/chunk_index, but changing AAD does not make nonce reuse safe. An observer can see old and current object versions for their own export; discarding an old manifest does not erase observed ciphertext. Retrying an export may lawfully use a new approved snapshot when source retractions changed its content. That is not itself a violation.
R5. A signed export must bind the complete ORDERED sequence and cardinality of chunks. A client must not turn a three-chunk export into a four-chunk export by repeating a valid chunk. Cryptographic hash collision resistance is guaranteed; structural ambiguity in tree encoding still matters.
R6. Restoration may write only inside the selected local directory, including through intermediate path components. Archive entries cannot be symlinks and cannot contain '..', absolute paths, NUL or drive prefixes; these validations are verified. Existing filesystem directories can contain symlinks installed by another local process. File creation must remain contained even with such existing symlinks and relevant path replacement races.
R7. Signing keys rotate every 8h. Tokens may live 24h from issuance. In absence of explicit revocation, every unexpired legitimate token must remain verifiable. Retiring an old signing key from new issuance does not revoke its existing tokens. Verification-key retention must cover the longest token expiry actually possible under that key. Explicit revocation is handled separately and correctly.
R8. CSV values are data, never spreadsheet formulas. The specified downstream SheetReader first skips leading spaces, tabs and carriage returns for formula detection, then treats leading '=', '+', '-', '@' as executable formulas. A leading apostrophe makes the entire cell literal. RFC-compliant CSV quoting does NOT change this consumer rule. The data can contain these leading characters. These are the agreed consumer semantics, not a request to guess behavior of another spreadsheet product.

## Baseline guarantees
G1. Session authentication, token signature verification, constant-time comparisons, expiry checks using UTC, tenant/project claim decoding and current revocation-list reads are runtime validated and correct. Token algorithms are allowlisted; unknown key IDs fail closed; no algorithm confusion exists. Download verification includes the signed tenant/export/snapshot/root fields before reading bytes. Key material and random nonces are not logged.
G2. canonical_query(validated_query) is a verified unambiguous encoding including tenant/project/filters/columns/order. sha256 and HMAC signatures are correct. The cursor contains query_hash signed at issuance. The request.query_hash field is arbitrary client input. Request.filter and request.columns are structurally validated but are not automatically equated to the cursor's approved values. `project` and `tenant` claims match the authenticated request and stay fixed; broadening dates or columns within that project is still forbidden by R2.
G3. `authorize_current(user,project)` checks live permission state, including resource grants removed after issuance. `cache` is access-controlled storage, but any authenticated request reaches E2. Cache keys already contain tenant, user, export ID and content version; the same user is allowed to request the same key after their project grant is revoked. Current policy revision is not part of that key.
G4. AEAD helpers correctly implement AES-GCM, a 12-byte nonce and authenticated decryption. export_nonce_prefix is 8 random bytes persisted with the export key. chunk_index is a 32-bit counter. For a new attempt, selected plaintext rows may change but export key/prefix are reused. Object uploads are atomic, but process crashes can occur after upload and before checkpoint persistence; old object versions remain observable.
G5. Merkle leaves are H('leaf'||chunk_digest); parents are H('node'||left||right). At an odd level, the final node is duplicated before pairing. The implementation recomputes this tree correctly. Signature binds tenant/export/snapshot/root, but NOT chunk_count or the ordered manifest itself. chunk_count is an unsigned manifest field. The verifier recomputes the root from the supplied list and checks the signature. It does not independently reject duplicate chunk indexes or references; each entry uses its own authenticated chunk_index when decrypting.
G6. Archive entry validation and the RFC CSV writer are correct. selected_root is an absolute path to an existing directory. `absolute()` is lexical normalization, does not resolve symlinks; `is_relative_to` compares lexical path components. The restoration process has ordinary user filesystem access. Permissions of directories outside selected_root are not a containment defense.
G7. UTC clocks, key IDs and signing-time routing are correct. Each key signs for 8h after creation, then a fresh key signs new tokens; token.exp = issue_time+24h. A token can be issued immediately before the old key stops signing. Token lifetime is not shortened by the rotation. Old verification keys are available until cleanup E8 deletes them.

## Candidate code and protocol
E2 read_export(req):
    user = authenticate(req)
    cursor = verify_signature_expiry_and_revocation(req.cursor)
    key = (cursor.tenant,user.id,cursor.export_id,cursor.content_version)
    if cache.contains(key): return cache[key]
    authorize_current(user,cursor.project)
    result = build_export(cursor,req)
